pool.text: A linear map \( T \) satisfies \( T\langle -1, -1 \rangle=\langle 0, -2 \rangle \) and \( T\langle 0, -1 \rangle=\langle 2, -1 \rangle \). Find \( T\langle 2, -3 \rangle \).
pool.sol: Write \( \langle 2, -3 \rangle=c_1\langle -1, -1 \rangle+c_2\langle 0, -1 \rangle \) with \( (c_1,c_2)=\langle -2, 5 \rangle \). By linearity, \( T\langle 2, -3 \rangle=c_1\langle 0, -2 \rangle+c_2\langle 2, -1 \rangle=\langle 10, -1 \rangle \).

pool.text: \( T(\mathbf x)=A\mathbf x \) with \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}0 & -1 & 3\\-1 & -3 & -1\\2 & 5 & 5\\2 & 8 & -4\end{matrix}\right] \). Which describes \( T \)?
pool.sol: \( \operatorname{rank}A=2 \). \( T \) is one-to-one iff rank = number of columns (3) and onto iff rank = number of rows (4). So it is neither one-to-one nor onto.

pool.text: Find the least-squares line for the points \( \left( -1, \  4\right) \), \( \left( 1, \  -2\right) \), \( \left( 2, \  -1\right) \).
pool.sol: Solve the normal equations \( A^TA\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}=A^T\mathbf y \) with \( A^TA=\left[\begin{matrix}3 & 2\\2 & 6\end{matrix}\right] \), \( A^T\mathbf y=\langle 1, -8 \rangle \): \( \hat\beta_0=\frac{11}{7},\ \hat\beta_1=- \frac{13}{7} \).
